entries.description: show list of models in cache
entries.notes: Lists mlxcel's own model store (the <root>/<owner>/<name> snapshots `crate::downloader::models_root` resolves) in b10621's exact output shape: a `number of models in cache: N` header then `%4zu. %s` per entry, then exit 0. Each entry is the repository id `-m` accepts. The b10621 short spelling `-cl` is accepted through the argv pre-pass in `src/cli/llama_short_flags.rs`, so it is not a clap spelling and is not claimed here.

entries.description: print source-able bash completion script for llama.cpp
entries.notes: Prints a source-able bash completion script generated from the live clap surface and exits 0, in b10621's script shape (one completion function, an `opts` list, a `case "$prev"` block giving path completion to the file-valued options, then `complete -F`). Only visible arguments and visible aliases reach the script: mlxcel's hidden b10621 compatibility surface and the `--dump-flag-surface` machine interface are deliberately omitted, which upstream has no equivalent of because llama.cpp hides no arguments. `mlxcel-server` registers the script against `mlxcel-server` and `mlxcel serve` against `mlxcel`, where b10621 registers one script against every llama.cpp executable.

entries.description: use default EmbeddingGemma model (note: can download weights from the internet)
entries.notes: The preset points `params.model.hf_repo` at the GGUF repository ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300M-qat-q4_0-GGUF and then overwrites the port, context, batch, parallelism and (for the gpt-oss presets) sampling block. mlxcel serves MLX SafeTensors and has no GGUF reader, so honoring only the checkpoint would drop the parameter block and honoring only the parameter block would serve a different quantization than the flag names. The option is accepted by the parser, hidden, and refused before the model reference is resolved, with a diagnostic naming the nearest MLX checkpoint (mlx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-4bit) and the exact `mlxcel download` and `mlxcel-server -m` command lines that reach it. The MLX target is named in the diagnostic only and is never resolved implicitly.
divergence: b10621 downloads ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300M-qat-q4_0-GGUF and serves it with the preset's parameter block; mlxcel refuses the flag at startup and names the MLX equivalent instead (#1448).

entries.description: print usage and exit
entries.notes: Both binaries print clap-generated help. Since #1448 the b10621 twin spelling `--usage` is accepted too: clap's generated help argument cannot carry an alias through the derive, so both server surfaces declare the option by hand under `disable_help_flag`, first in the struct so it lands before any `next_help_heading` group. `mlxcel serve --usage` and `mlxcel-server --usage` both render help and exit 0.

entries.description: Set colored logging ('on', 'off', or 'auto', default: 'auto') 'auto' enables colors when output is to a terminal (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_COLORS)
entries.notes: Values are parsed with b10621's own case-sensitive vocabulary (`common_arg_utils::is_truthy` / `is_falsey` / `is_autoy`), not clap's wider boolish set, and an unrecognized value stops startup. `auto` colors only when the sink is a terminal, so `--log-file` never receives ANSI escapes.

entries.description: Log disable
entries.notes: Wins over every other logging option and installs no subscriber at all, matching b10621's `common_log_pause`. See `src/server/logging.rs` for the destination precedence it heads.

entries.description: Log to file (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_FILE)
entries.notes: Since #1448 the file is created `0600` (an existing file is tightened to `0600`), a symlinked destination is refused, and an unusable destination stops startup instead of silently falling back to the terminal. That check runs before the model reference resolves, so it costs no download. Every line is scanned for registered credentials (`--api-key`, `--api-key-file`, `--hf-token`, `HF_TOKEN`, `LLAMA_API_KEY`) and redacted. Destination precedence is `--log-disable`, then `--log-file`, then `LLAMA_ARG_LOG_FILE`, then the mlxcel-native `LLAMA_LOG_FILE`, then stdout.

entries.description: Enable prefix in log messages (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_PREFIX)
entries.notes: b10621's prefix is the per-line level tag, verified against the pinned macOS arm64 binary: `--no-log-prefix` drops the `I` / `W` character and keeps the component tag. mlxcel maps the pair onto the tracing formatter's level field, on by default as upstream. The environment binding is resolved at runtime rather than through clap so b10621's `parse_bool_value` vocabulary and the `LLAMA_ARG_NO_LOG_PREFIX` alias both hold; clap's boolish parser accepts a wider set and errors outside it.

entries.description: Log prompts to directory (auto-created if not present; only used for debugging, default: disabled)
entries.notes: mlxcel does not write request prompts to disk. Accepting the flag as a no-op would leave the named directory empty while the operator believed prompts were being captured, and implementing it would create a plaintext copy of user request bodies on the log volume, a disclosure surface the project declines to add for a debugging aid. The option is accepted by the parser, hidden, and refused before the model reference is resolved, with a diagnostic naming `--log-file` plus `--verbosity 4` as the request-level debugging path that records metadata and no prompt bodies. Unlike b10621, which creates the directory from inside its parser, the refusal leaves no trace on the filesystem.
divergence: b10621 records every request prompt under the named directory; mlxcel refuses the option at startup and writes no prompt log (#1448).

entries.description: Enable timestamps in log messages (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_TIMESTAMPS)
entries.notes: On by default, as b10621's llama-server is (verified against the pinned macOS arm64 binary). Resolved through the same runtime bool-pair path as `--log-prefix`, so `LLAMA_ARG_NO_LOG_TIMESTAMPS` and b10621's truthiness vocabulary both hold.

entries.description: enable default speculative decoding config
entries.notes: b10621's default speculative configuration enables its n-gram-modulo drafter, which predicts continuations from the context itself with no draft checkpoint. mlxcel's drafters are checkpoint-backed (`--draft-kind mtp` on an MTP-capable target, `--draft-kind dflash --model-draft <path-or-repo-id>` otherwise), so there is nothing for the flag to configure. It is accepted by the parser, hidden, and refused before the model reference is resolved, with a diagnostic naming both mlxcel drafters. The n-gram tuning knobs it would have set are classified under #1433 in the speculative shard.
divergence: b10621 enables its n-gram-modulo drafter; mlxcel has no context-only drafter and refuses the flag at startup (#1448).

entries.description: Set verbosity level to infinity (i.e. log all messages, useful for debugging)
entries.notes: Both b10621 spellings are accepted since #1448 (`--log-verbose` is a visible clap alias), and the flag is unconditional as upstream's is: a command-line `--verbose` now beats `RUST_LOG`, where before #1448 `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env` ran first and `RUST_LOG=warn mlxcel-server -v` silently ignored the flag. `--verbose` resolves to the same filter as the top `--verbosity` tier, so it is never less verbose than `--verbosity 5`, mirroring b10621's `verbosity = INT_MAX`.

entries.description: Set the verbosity threshold. Messages with a higher verbosity will be ignored. Values: - 0: generic output - 1: error - 2: warning - 3: info - 4: trace (more info) - 5: debug (default: 3) (env: LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY)
entries.notes: Threshold semantics match: messages above the threshold are dropped, so a larger number is always at least as verbose, and the default is b10621's 3. The tiers map onto mlxcel's own levels (0 and 1 error, 2 warn, 3 info, 4 debug, 5 and above trace for mlxcel's targets over debug for dependencies). A command-line value beats `RUST_LOG`; `LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY` does not. See `src/server/logging.rs` for the full precedence. The b10621 short spelling `-lv` is accepted through the argv pre-pass in `src/cli/llama_short_flags.rs`, so it is not a clap spelling and is not claimed here.

entries.description: show version and build info
entries.notes: `mlxcel-server --version` always answered this; since #1448 `propagate_version` on the `mlxcel` root command carries it onto the `serve` subcommand too, so the b10621 spelling works on both server surfaces rather than one.
